A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SoftCVI work, with readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The new Appendix A.4 in v4 accounts for subsequent appendix renumbering; the earlier experimental material remains available for comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original Bayesian inference comparisons in Sections 4–5, alongside appendix results on gradient signal-to-noise ratios, MNIST variational autoencoders, and Bayesian neural additive models.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including Figures 1–10 and Table 1. Their retention from v3 does not alter their status as original results of the work.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the cross-entropy objective, and the implemented model adaptations are unchanged. Alternative f-divergences are discussed as future possibilities, and the stop-gradient convention clarified in Appendix A.2 was already specified in v3.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Eight Schools, linear regression, SLCP, GARCH, the toy Gaussian gradient task, MNIST autoencoders, and synthetic Bayesian neural additive regression. The new divergence discussion introduces no evaluated task or scenario.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: ELBO and SNIS-fKL remain in the main and neural additive comparisons, ELBO in the autoencoder comparison, and SNIS-fKL in the gradient analysis. No alternative divergence is newly evaluated.

E3.justification: The main experiments retain K = 8 and 50,000 Adam steps. Appendix sample-count sweeps, autoencoder training settings, neural additive data splits and widths, and evaluation metrics are also unchanged.

E4.justification: The gradient signal-to-noise analysis, negative-distribution comparisons, sensitivity to K, and posterior case studies are retained unchanged. Appendix A.4 adds discussion and formulas, without a new ablation or robustness test.

E5.justification: Both versions report 50 independent runs per main task and objective, and 10 differently initialized neural additive networks. Table 1 retains the same plus-minus reporting, and plotted variability and statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Figures 1–10 and all numerical entries in Table 1 are unchanged, as are their reported qualitative findings. This includes the neural additive comparison in which ELBO achieves the highest test log-likelihood. No results accompany the proposed alternative divergences.

T1.justification: The new Appendix A.4 defines categorical f-divergences, including convexity and f(1) = 0 conditions, and gives a short KL/cross-entropy derivation. This is a limited formal addition; the posterior-recovery and gradient-variance results remain unchanged. Appendix A.2 clarifies the existing derivation without changing its conclusion.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: contrastive variational objectives, posterior recovery, zero gradient variance at the optimum, and competitive mass-covering inference. Expanded future directions do not change the claimed demonstrated contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix A.4 adds a task-dependent rationale for divergence choice, suggesting that more mode-seeking objectives may suit generative modeling when uncertainty quantification is less critical. The conclusion also emphasizes future control of posterior calibration. Existing interpretations and failure conditions are retained.

D1.justification: Implementation settings, software disclosures, hardware and runtime information, and code-access links are unchanged. Appendix A.2 repeats and explains the stop-gradient requirement already documented in Section 2.3, rather than disclosing a new implementation requirement.

R1.justification: v4 adds Ali and Silvey (1966) and Csiszár (1967) to support the f-divergence discussion. These are limited citation additions; the existing positioning relative to variational inference and contrastive learning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 expands Section 2.2, inserts Appendix A.4, rewrites the normalization-gradient explanation and future-work paragraph, and updates acknowledgments. Subsequent appendix and equation references are renumbered. These are localized changes within the retained overall narrative.

P2.justification: Existing appendix material reflows: Figure 5 moves from before Table 1 to after it, and Figure 6 moves onto the page containing its explanatory discussion. Figure artwork, axes, legends, captions, and table structure remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 modestly improves clarity by making the categorical-divergence interpretation explicit and explaining the existing stop-gradient convention directly within Appendix A.2's derivation. Appendix A.4 supplies mathematical context while clearly reserving alternative objectives for future work. The empirical evidence and core conclusions are unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
